question.text: Section 15 of SCRA requires a stockbroker entering into a contract as a principal with a non-member to:

answer.text: Only inform SEBI of the transaction
Secure written consent within 3 days from the date of the contract and disclose on the contract note that he is acting as principal
Only obtain approval from the stock exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 15 permits a stockbroker to enter into a contract as a principal with another person only if written consent is received from that person within three days from the date of the contract, and disclosure is made on the contract note that the broker is acting as principal. The Trap: Verbal consent or simply informing SEBI is not sufficient; the section specifically requires written consent within 3 days plus disclosure on the contract note. Note: Anchor Section 15 to two requirements: written consent within 3 days and disclosure of principal capacity on the contract note.
